{{Short description|1st stage of the 2018 Copa Sudamericana}}
The '''2018 Copa Sudamericana first stage''' was played from 13 February to 23 May 2018.<ref name="calendar">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/calendario_2018_cla_cs.pdf|title=EL CALENDARIO DE AMBOS TORNEOS|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref> A total of 44 teams competed in the first stage to decide 22 of the 32 places in the [[2018 Copa Sudamericana second stage|second stage]] of the [[2018 Copa Sudamericana]].<ref name="regulations">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/reglamento-conmebol-sudamericana-2018-espanol_0.pdf|title=Reglamento CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2018|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|language=Spanish}}</ref>

==Draw==
<section begin=Draw />
The draw for the first stage was held on 20 December 2017, 20:00 [[Time in Paraguay|PYST]] ([[UTC−03:00|UTC−3]]), at the CONMEBOL Convention Centre in [[Luque]], [[Paraguay]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/proceso-de-acreditacion-medios-de-prensa-para-el-sorteo-de-la-conmebol-libertadores-y-conmebol|title=Proceso de acreditación a medios de prensa para el sorteo de la CONMEBOL Libertadores y CONMEBOL Sudamericana|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=12 December 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/los-cruces-de-la-conmebol-sudamericana|title=Los cruces de la CONMEBOL Sudamericana|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=20 December 2017}}</ref> For the first stage, the teams were divided into two pots according to their geographical zones:
*'''Pot A (South Zone):''' 22 teams from Argentina, Bolivia, Chile, Paraguay, and Uruguay
*'''Pot B (North Zone):''' 22 teams from Brazil, Colombia, Ecuador, Peru, and Venezuela

The 44 teams were drawn into 22 ties (E1–E22) between a team from Pot A and a team from Pot B, with the teams from Pot B hosting the second leg in odd-numbered ties, and the teams from Pot A hosting the second leg in even-numbered ties. This distribution ensured that teams from the same association could not be drawn into the same tie.<ref name="draw system">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/sorteos_libertadores_sudamericana_2018_.pdf|title=Esquema de sorteo de la CONMEBOL Libertadores y la CONMEBOL Sudamericana 2018|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref><section end=Draw />

==Format==
<section begin=Format />
In the first stage, each tie was played on a home-and-away [[two-legged tie|two-legged]] basis. If tied on aggregate, the [[away goals rule]] would be used. If still tied, [[extra time (association football)|extra time]] would not be played, and the [[penalty shoot-out (association football)|penalty shoot-out]] would be used to determine the winner (Regulations Article 27).<ref name="regulations"/>

The 22 winners of the first stage advanced to the second stage to join the 10 teams transferred from the [[2018 Copa Libertadores|Copa Libertadores]] (two [[2018 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages#Copa Sudamericana qualification|best teams]] eliminated in the [[2018 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages#Third stage|third stage]] of [[2018 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages|qualifying]] and eight third-placed teams in the [[2018 Copa Libertadores group stage|group stage]]).<section end=Format />

==Matches==
The first legs were played on 13, 15, 20–22 February, 10–12 and 18 April, and the second legs were played on 6–8 March, 8–10 and 23 May 2018.<ref name="fixture">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/es/programa-de-partidos-de-la-conmebol-sudamericana-2018|title=Programa de partidos de la CONMEBOL SUDAMERICANA 2018|publisher=CONMEBOL.com|date=21 December 2017}}</ref><ref name="fixture_pdf">{{cite web|url=http://www.conmebol.com/sites/default/files/programa_de_partidos_conmebol_sudamericana_2018.pdf|title=PROGRAMA DE PARTIDOS CONMEBOL SUDAMERICANA 2018|publisher=CONMEBOL.com}}</ref>
